doc.title: Holly Hofmann interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: San Diego and working as a flutist
title: Constantly learning repertoire
summary: She keeps learning tunes, noting pianist Mike Wofford knows everything, and rearranges standards.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: And when you say you travel, you get thrown in with other people, other rhythm sections, and like most of the people we were talking about that are here for this jazz party, a big part of — one thing that I think students need to know about being a jazz musician is a big part of it is knowing repertory. Is that something you’re constantly working on?

Just when I think I know a lot of tunes, I run into somebody who knows double the tunes I know. Like Mike Wofford is a good example. There’s not a tune you can call out that Mike doesn’t know. So yeah I’m constantly learning tunes, constantly writing, constantly rearranging old standards that are still great tunes, into maybe a little bit different groove or just a different way of playing the tune, to make it fresh.
